The 1 to 7 bytes after byte 3, as given by Size of Address Field, carry the source and destination addresses.
The D_PDU type-specific header part is as specified for each type in this annex.
The last two bytes of every header hold the CRC computed per C.4.2.8.

The remaining 8 bits of the EOW (bits 7-0) hold the type-specific EOW data.
EOW mapping: EOW bits 11-8 go in header byte 0 bits 3-0 (EOW MSB at byte 0 bit 3); EOW bits 7-0 go in header byte 1 bits 7-0 (EOW LSB at byte 1 bit 0).
The 8-bit EOT field approximates the time remaining in the current transmission of the sending node.

Size of Header gives h, the header length in bytes, counting the type, EOW, EOT, size byte, type-specific header and header CRC.
Size of Header excludes the address field.

notes: Header byte 3 = 0x47: m = 2, h = 7.

requirement: Every D_PDU sent carries both source and destination address, each taking half the address field bits.
The first half of the address field is the destination address.
The second half of the address field is the source address.
For odd m the middle address byte is shared: destination in its high nibble, source in its low nibble (Figure C-4(a)); for even m each address takes m/2 whole bytes (Figure C-4(b), p.C-15).
notes: Figure C-4 labels the last address row 4+m; the address ends at byte 3+m (Figure C-2, worked example p.C-19).

requirement: Addresses are binary numbers, from 4 bits up to 28 bits (3.5 bytes) each.
Each byte or fractional byte of an address is represented by a decimal number (dotted decimal).
The binary value of each dotted-decimal number is mapped into the corresponding byte.
Unicast (node) addresses run from 0.0.0.0 to 15.255.255.255.
For D_PDUs supporting group addressing (types 7 and 8), the group flag is treated as a 29th address bit, giving group addresses 16.0.0.0 to 31.255.255.255.
The broadcast (all stations) address is group address 31.255.255.255.
A fractional-byte part of an address maps to the leftmost non-zero number of the dotted-decimal form.
The other dotted-decimal numbers refer to whole-byte parts of the address.
Example: with 3.5-byte addresses written w.x.y.z, w ranges 0 to 15 and carries the top bits; z carries the bottom 8 bits.

Address bits are placed with the address MSB in the MSB of the first byte of its field and the LSB in the LSB of the last byte, per Figure C-4(a) for 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 bytes and Figure C-4(b) for 1, 2, 3 bytes.
When any field spans several octets, bit significance decreases as octet number increases (most significant part in the first octet).
notes: General rule; see interp C-0134.

requirement: The lowest numbered bit of a field holds its lowest order value.
Leading zero address bytes may be omitted, keeping source and destination the same length.
Trailing zero address bytes are always sent.
Worked example: m = 2 with destination 0.0.0.5 and source 0.0.0.100 gives address bytes 0x05 0x64.

requirement: The bytes after the address field encode the type-specific header defined in C.4.4 to C.4.15.
The header has its own 2-byte CRC so that a valid header can be used even when the data part is corrupt.
The two bytes after the type-specific header hold a 16-bit CRC.
The header CRC polynomial is x^16+x^15+x^12+x^11+x^8+x^6+x^3+1 (0x19949), computed by the V.41 Appendix I shift-register method or an equivalent software method.
notes: Not the V.41 polynomial.

requirement: The header CRC shift register starts at all zeros.
The header CRC covers every header bit except the sync: type, EOW, EOT, both size fields, addresses and the type-specific header.
A header with a valid CRC is processed whatever the result of the CRC on any segmented C_PDU in the same D_PDU.
CRC bits map into the CRC bytes with the CRC MSB in the LSB of the first CRC byte and the CRC LSB in the MSB of the last, so the CRC goes out MSB first as V.42 8.1.2.3 requires.

requirement: Type 10 layout: bytes 4+m and 5+m RX LWE (16 bits); byte 6+m bit 7 Encoding, bits 6-0 Offset; byte 7+m Ack Length (aa); then Ack Data of 0 to 21 bytes in the header; or, in the long form, Ack Data after the header CRC followed by a 32-bit CRC on the Ack Data.

requirement: ACK-ONLY is the selective acknowledgement for received DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK D_PDUs, used when the node has no segments of its own to send or (Ed4 only) when the acks will not fit in a DATA-ACK.
ACK-ONLY carries the fields of Figure C-11 or C-12: at least RECEIVE LOWER WINDOW EDGE.
RX LWE equals the sequence number at the RX LWE pointer of the node's receive window.
RX LWE is modulo 256 for type 1 and modulo 65536 for type 10.
notes: Unnumbered shall.

requirement: ED3-ACK-ONLY (type 1) carries the SELECTIVE ACKS field, mapped per Figure C-11.
SELECTIVE ACKS (0 to 16 bytes) is a bitmap of the status of every D_PDU from the receive window LWE up to and including its UWE; its length comes from Size of Header, not an explicit field.
A set bit in SELECTIVE ACKS is a positive acknowledgement: that FSN was received correctly.
A D_PDU gets a positive ack only if its segment CRC checks; a good header CRC alone is not enough.
D_PDUs with DROP C_PDU set are acknowledged positively whatever their data CRC result.
A clear bit in SELECTIVE ACKS is a negative acknowledgement: that FSN was received in error or not at all.
SELECTIVE ACKS is built and mapped per Figures C-13 and C-14 and the rules below.
The LSB of the first SELECTIVE ACKS byte stands for FSN RX LWE + 1; the RX LWE bit itself is always 0 and is not sent.
Each following bit stands for the next FSN in ascending order, with no FSN skipped.
notes: Figure C-14: bits fill each byte from bit 0 to bit 7.

requirement: The bit for the receive window UWE lies in the last SELECTIVE ACKS byte.
Any bits in the last byte above the UWE bit are padded with zero.
No SELECTIVE ACKS bytes follow the byte holding the UWE bit.
Type 10 offers two Ack Data encodings for large windows; acknowledgements may be spread over several ACK-ONLY D_PDUs.
Keep each ACK-ONLY D_PDU small to reduce the risk of losing it.
Send ACK-ONLY D_PDUs more than once, since lost acknowledgements cause delay and needless retransmission.
When a set of one or more ACK-ONLY D_PDUs is sent, together they acknowledge every received DATA D_PDU; their number and encoding are the implementation's choice.
notes: Unnumbered shall.

requirement: Type 10 positively acknowledges only D_PDUs with a correct segmented C_PDU CRC.
notes: Repeats C.4.5.4 (6) for type 10.

requirement: Type 10 positively acknowledges D_PDUs with DROP C_PDU set whatever their data CRC.
notes: Repeats C.4.5.4 (7) for type 10.

requirement: If the Ack Data fits in 21 bytes or fewer, the Figure C-1(a) header-only form is used with all Ack Data in the header.
If the Ack Data is longer than 21 bytes, the Figure C-1(b) form with two CRCs is used and no Ack Data is put in the header.
In that long form all Ack Data follows the header, after the header CRC.
The largest window means up to 32768 D_PDUs to acknowledge (up to 4096 bitmap bytes).
Offset is 7 bits; Offset x 256 gives the distance in D_PDUs (bits) from the LWE where this D_PDU's Ack Data starts; several ACK-ONLY D_PDUs with different offsets may together cover the window.
notes: See interp C-0233.

requirement: Ack Length gives the Ack Data size in bytes, up to 255.
A sender may use either Ack Data encoding, or both.
Evaluate both encodings and send the more compact.
notes: Repeated on p.C-32.

requirement: A receiver supports both Ack Data encodings.
notes: Unnumbered shall; sentence ends on p.C-32.

requirement: Encoding bit 0: bitmap per C.4.5.4, a 1 meaning the D_PDU was accepted, starting from the first D_PDU after the offset point; trailing zero padding to a whole byte is safe.
Encoding bit 1: run length encoding (RLE) applied to the standard bitmap of C.4.5.4.
notes: Value 1 for RLE is implied, not stated.

requirement: RLE one-byte code: bit 7 Value, bit 6 Extended = 0, bits 5-0 Length.
RLE two-byte code: byte 0 bit 7 Value, bit 6 Extended = 1, 14-bit Length from byte 0 bit 5 (MSB) to byte 1 bit 0 (LSB).
Value is the repeated bit value; Length is the number of repeats, so a code covers Length + 1 bits (Length 0 = the value once).
RLE codes follow one another through the whole Ack Data.

requirement: RESET/WIN-RESYNC controls resynchronisation or reinitialisation of the selective ARQ protocol on the link between two nodes.
Reset and resynchronisation act on the TX LWE and RX LWE of the sending and receiving windows, as specified in C.7.2.
RESET/WIN-RESYNC uses the stop-and-wait (IRQ) protocol.
Receiving a RESET/WIN-RESYNC causes the receiver to send an acknowledgement, itself a RESET/WIN-RESYNC D_PDU.
Sending of regular-data D_PDUs (DATA-ONLY, ACK-ONLY, DATA-ACK) is suspended until any RESET/WIN-RESYNC stop-and-wait exchange completes.
RESET/WIN-RESYNC carries FULL RESET COMMAND, RESET TX WIN RQST, RESET RX WIN CMND, RESET ACK, NEW RECEIVE LWE and RESET FRAME ID NUMBER, mapped per Figure C-19 (and C-20).
FULL RESET COMMAND = 1 forces a full reset of the ARQ machines at both ends to their initial values (C.7.2, C.7.3).
Setting RESET TX WIN RQST asks the peer to resynchronise the data TX-LWE and RX-LWE pointers at both ends.
A node receiving RESET TX WIN RQST = 1 answers by forcing window resynchronisation with a RESET/WIN-RESYNC carrying RESET RX WIN CMND.
RESET RX WIN CMND = 1 forces resynchronisation of the sender's TX-LWE and the receiver's RX-LWE.
notes: Unnumbered shall (10).

requirement: A node sending RESET RX WIN CMND = 1 sets NEW RECEIVE LWE to its own TX-LWE.
A node sending RESET RX WIN CMND = 1 then waits for a RESET/WIN-RESYNC with RESET ACK = 1 confirming the resynchronisation.
A node receiving RESET RX WIN CMND = 1 sets its TX LWE to the received NEW RECEIVE LWE.
notes: As printed; see interp C-0274.

requirement: A node receiving RESET RX WIN CMND = 1 then sends a RESET/WIN-RESYNC with RESET ACK = 1.
RESET ACK = 1 acknowledges the most recently received RESET/WIN-RESYNC.
A node may use its RESET ACK D_PDU to also request or force reset or resync of its own ARQ variables, for example when both data directions need it.
NEW RECEIVE LWE is valid only when RESET RX WIN CMND = 1.
NEW RECEIVE LWE is ignored in every other case.
The DTS uses RESET FRAME ID NUMBER to recognise a copy of a RESET/WIN-RESYNC it has already received.
RESET FRAME ID NUMBER is a unique integer assigned in ascending order (with wrap) and not reused until the D_PDU carrying it has been acknowledged.
GAP: the RESET FRAME ID modulus is only 'appropriate modulo'. Reading: modulo 256, the size of its 8-bit field in both types 3 and 12.

CONFLICT: the RESET RX WIN CMND rules disagree on direction: the sender puts its own TX-LWE in NEW RECEIVE LWE (p.C-38), but the receiver is told to set its TX LWE from it (p.C-39), while the field name and the flag's definition point to the receiver's RX LWE. Reading to be fixed by a worked two-node scenario test before implementation and recorded here.
notes: Plan 4.4. Pages C-38 to C-39.

notes: Unnumbered shall (2).

The type 4 segmented C_PDU immediately follows the header.

C_PDUs on the expedited delivery service travel in EXPEDITED-DATA-ONLY and EXPEDITED-ACK-ONLY D_PDUs.

requirement: MANAGEMENT (type 6) carries EOW messages or M_PDUs when the sender needs explicit acknowledgement of receipt.
Repeat MANAGEMENT D_PDUs when sending them; they bypass other D_PDUs to arrive quickly.
notes: Phrased as a recommendation.

requirement: A DTS acknowledges a received MANAGEMENT D_PDU by sending a MANAGEMENT D_PDU with ACK = 1.
MANAGEMENT D_PDUs jump the queue: they are processed and sent ahead of every other pending D_PDU type.
MANAGEMENT D_PDUs are stop-and-wait: at most one unacknowledged MANAGEMENT D_PDU at any time.
MANAGEMENT carries EXTENDED MESSAGE, VALID MESSAGE, ACK, MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER and EXTENDED MANAGEMENT MESSAGE, mapped per Figure C-23.

VALID MESSAGE = 0 when the EOW field holds an EOW that needs no acknowledgement.
A MANAGEMENT D_PDU with VALID MESSAGE = 0 is used only to acknowledge another MANAGEMENT D_PDU.
EXTENDED MESSAGE = 1 when the D_PDU carries a non-empty EXTENDED MANAGEMENT MESSAGE field.
With EXTENDED MESSAGE = 0 the EXTENDED MANAGEMENT MESSAGE field is absent.
MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER holds an integer from 0 to 255.
notes: Split: shall (12), identification by this number, is C-1014.

requirement: The DTS keeps variables for MANAGEMENT frame ID numbers.
TX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER holds the frame ID for MANAGEMENT D_PDUs being sent.
RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER holds the frame ID of the most recently received MANAGEMENT D_PDU.
On initialisation (for example a new connection) TX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER is set to 0.
On initialisation RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER is set to an out-of-range value above 255.
Each unique MANAGEMENT D_PDU sent carries the current TX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER.
TX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER increments by one modulo 256 after each use, except when repeated copies of the D_PDU are to be sent.
Repeated copies of a MANAGEMENT D_PDU keep the same frame ID number.
The DTS compares the frame ID of each received MANAGEMENT D_PDU with RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER.
A received MANAGEMENT D_PDU whose frame ID differs from RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER is treated as new.
notes: Split: shall (23), updating the variable, is C-1015.

requirement: A received MANAGEMENT D_PDU whose frame ID equals RX MANAGEMENT FRAME ID NUMBER is taken as a repeat of one already received.

Type 7 C_PDU ID numbers (0 to 4095) form a space separate from type 8 C_PDU ID numbers.

notes: Unnumbered shall, condition 1.

TX LWE is the lowest-numbered outstanding unacknowledged D_PDU, in modulo terms

requirement: A configured maximum transmission length must never block one D_PDU, but how far a transmission may then exceed it is NOT STATED. Reading: when the first D_PDU the build would take does not fit within the configured length, the transmission is made exactly the whole modem blocks that D_PDU needs; other D_PDUs may use what is left of those blocks, and nothing else lengthens it. A D_PDU that needs more than 127.5 s on the waveform in use cannot be sent, which is a configuration error
notes: C-0551, C-0878, K-0094, K-0095; refines core-architecture.md 5.3, which let other D_PDUs fill up to 127.5 s

requirement: EOT counts from the start of the D_PDU, but where a D_PDU starts on air inside an interleaved modem block is NOT STATED. Reading: a D_PDU starts on air at the start of the block holding its first byte (preamble plus whole blocks before it), the earliest instant any of its bits is sent, so its EOT and reception window are never early
notes: C-0104, C-0350, C-0891, D-0017; core-architecture.md 5.6 and section 10 item 4

requirement: A non-ARQ request in EXPEDITED-DATA(UNCONNECTED) waits until the expedited transmission completes (C-0615, C-0737), but when that is reached is NOT STATED. Reading: a type 7 C_PDU is not placed in a transmission while an expedited C_PDU to the same destination is still waiting to be placed; it may go in the same transmission after the last of them
notes: C-0615, C-0737, C-0288. Per destination because the unconnected DTS state is kept per peer (C-0565 to C-0568; core-architecture.md 4.2); Table C-13 itself says all expedited data
